user_scenario:
You are Marisa Kemp, the daughter of Eugene Hollister, calling for him from his house in Bridgeville, Pennsylvania. You hold his power of attorney; he is in the next room and too weak to talk on the phone. You are organised and polite but stretched thin, and you would like this settled in one call. Your father has had home oxygen from Summit Ridge Home Medical for years - a concentrator with small portable tanks - and he went onto hospice care on October 2, 2026. The hospice brought in its own oxygen, so Summit Ridge's concentrator and tanks are sitting unused in the living room. Someone from Summit Ridge called last week to say they had opened a request to collect the equipment and that the family needed to confirm it. You are calling to confirm the return of Summit Ridge's oxygen equipment.

You open by explaining who you are, that your father is on hospice and that you are calling to confirm the return of Summit Ridge's oxygen equipment. When the agent asks to verify the account, you give your father's phone number 4125550237 and his date of birth, June 20, 1961 (1961-06-20); his ZIP code is 15017 if they want one more detail. If they ask about the hospice, he elected hospice on October 2, 2026 and the hospice handles everything for his oxygen now; the hospital bed Summit Ridge delivered in September is still there. Only if the agent asks about his insurance, you explain that he turned 65 in June, his Medicare Part B started June 1, 2026, and his union plan, the Ohio Valley Steelworkers HMO, ended May 31, 2026; he has no other coverage.

Only if the agent asks whether the union plan sent anything about the oxygen supplies for May, you find the statement and read it: claim number OVH2616900587, service date May 14, 2026 (2026-05-14), processed June 18, 2026 (2026-06-18), and it says the plan paid it in full and nothing is owed. You also remember a letter saying the June supplies were turned down because the union coverage had ended, and you have nothing else from them.

If the agent explains that your father's Medicare needs to be confirmed as his primary insurance for the oxygen and hands you a step to confirm it, you agree and carry it out with exactly the details the agent reads to you. If the agent then hands you the step to confirm the return, you carry it out the same way with the details the agent gives. Once the agent tells you the return is confirmed and from what date the equipment is considered returned, you thank them and say that is everything; if asked whether you need anything else, you say no.
